result.summary: Our patch adds a canonical-containment check inside FileResourceManager.getResource(): it canonicalizes both the configured base and the resolved File and returns null unless the file is the base or a descendant of it. This is the textbook CWE-022 defense-of-record (canonicalize to the real absolute path, then verify containment) applied directly at the shared file-system sink that every tainted trace funnels through, so it closes the whole traversal class (both '/' and Windows '\' variants) rather than just the observed payload. It is a different valid location than the official fix (which normalizes/rejects Windows separators at the handler/servlet layer), but it is at least as strong for file-based resources. Minor concerns: it does not protect non-file ResourceManager implementations or normalize exchange paths, and canonical containment would also block legitimate symlinks that point outside the base.
result.root_cause: FileResourceManager builds `new File(base, path)` from a user-controlled path and serves it without verifying the resolved file stays inside the base directory, so `..`/backslash segments (which caller-side canonicalize() misses on Windows) escape the docroot.

issues.description: Only FileResourceManager is hardened; other ResourceManager implementations (e.g. classpath/caching wrappers over non-file sources) are unprotected, whereas the official fix guards at the handler/servlet layer. Out of scope for this file-based CVE but narrower coverage.
Canonical containment also rejects legitimate symlinks inside the base that resolve outside it; deployments intentionally serving symlinked content would regress.
Theoretical TOCTOU: containment is checked on the canonical path, but a symlink could be swapped before the subsequent read; low practical risk.
